tools.name: Mizuchi

capabilities.purpose: Function-at-a-time matching-decompilation pipeline: optional m2c seed, project-script compilation, objdiff instruction comparison, Claude retry loop, and optional decomp-permuter.

target_architectures.x86_historical_compiler_support: No shipped or tested x86/MSC/Turbo C recipe; an arbitrary Bash compiler template could theoretically invoke an adapter.

capabilities.object_binary_formats: Mizuchi supplies paths to objdiff-wasm and GNU map/nm tooling; this inspected pipeline does not itself state or prove OMF, NE, MZ, COFF/PE or linker-format coverage.
capabilities.known_compiler: Yes, operationally: a project-provided compilerScript is the forward compiler; version, flags and runner are not modeled as first-class proof fields.
capabilities.compiler_specific_behavior: m2c/permuter target mappings and permuter compiler-type weights are encoded; no historical x86 compiler model is encoded.
capabilities.outputs_compilable_source: Yes, C code extracted from m2c, Claude, or permuter output and compiled as a temporary object.
capabilities.recompilation_feedback_loop: Yes. Claude receives compiler errors or full formatted objdiff result and can call a compile-and-view-assembly MCP tool during an attempt.
capabilities.automatic_retries: Yes; sequential Claude conversation retries up to maxRetries (example 25), with session resume, timeout policies and a generic stall prompt.
capabilities.candidate_comparison_score: Instruction-row differenceCount plus matchingCount; zero instruction differences is pipeline success. Permuter has its own score.
capabilities.structured_feedback: Partly: instruction strings and five mismatch categories (insertion/deletion/replacement/opcode/argument), compiler errors and scalar counts. No typed parent/candidate/oracle relation across proof dimensions.
capabilities.relocations_fixups: Not an explicit Mizuchi acceptance dimension. The example passes objdiff functionRelocDiffs: none; no OMF/NE fixup or relocation-order proof model is present.
capabilities.data_layout: No candidate data/static-layout comparison or ownership proof in the function pipeline.
capabilities.translation_unit_context: User getContextScript generates a header-like context and compiler prepends it to one candidate function. There is no whole-TU reconstruction/compilation state.
capabilities.cross_function_context: Atlas prompt builder can provide declarations, types, callers, similar matched examples and map-file lookup; this is prompt context, not compile-time predecessor/TU evidence.
capabilities.batch_candidate_exploration: No AI beam/batch. One background permuter task may run for each non-worse unique submitted C string while the sequential Claude loop continues.
capabilities.effective_output_deduplication: No. Background permuter deduplicates exact submitted C strings; Claude cache keys prompts/follow-ups. Neither clusters equivalent compiler outputs.
capabilities.ai_llms: Claude Agent SDK only in current built-in AI runner; default claude-sonnet-4-6 and configurable model, soft-timeout model/effort override.
capabilities.automation_human_loop: Normal pipeline is automated and Claude is restricted to Read/Glob/Grep plus one MCP compile/diff tool. Prompts/config/context and optional post-match integration are human/project supplied.
capabilities.history_provenance: JSON/HTML reports retain attempts, plugin results, timing and chat sections; claude-cache.json stores replayable conversation trees. It has no persistent compiler-mechanism/negative-evidence database.
capabilities.independent_acceptance: No built-in strict independent proof. Optional integrator can run a project verification script only after instruction-level success.

findings.claim: The live code runs setup context, optional m2c/compiler/objdiff and permuter programmatic stages, then sequential Claude/compiler/objdiff retries; a background permuter can terminate foreground work only with a perfect match.
Pipeline success is defined by zero formatted instruction-row differences for one named function symbol, not by an explicit whole-object/link/data/fixup proof contract.

Claude feedback is raw recovered assembly plus scalar/count-labelled instruction differences; retries remember a best count but do not use output clustering, a beam, typed mismatch mechanisms, or analysis-level escalation.
m2c is used as one initial candidate and the built-in adapter maps only ARM/MIPS/PowerPC families; no x86 historical-compiler implementation is present.

The author reports 74% average matching across three runs each of 30 selected Sonic Advance 3 and 30 Animal Forest functions, with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and 12 attempts; selection and context restrictions limit generalization.

A compact compiler-response envelope that preserves local strict evidence and effective-output identity would complement Mizuchi's agent loop; replacing local acceptance with Mizuchi would weaken observed Empires/Stunts/SimAnt/Icy Tower proof boundaries.

reuse_decision.decision: Learn from and potentially adapt isolated concepts; do not integrate as an acceptance system or add a production dependency now.
reuse_decision.license_dependency_note: Mizuchi is MIT, but direct reuse would also add Node, Anthropic Agent SDK, objdiff-wasm and m2c/decomp-permuter submodule dependency reviews.

limitations: The normal acceptance criterion is instruction-level named-symbol comparison rather than complete artifact proof.
No demonstrated historical x86 / MSC / Turbo C / OMF / NE adapter or test fixture.
No effective-output deduplication, multi-hypothesis beam, learned compiler rules, or persistent negative-evidence memory.
Context is user-provided header text; original translation-unit composition and linker environment are outside the pipeline.
Function prompts are processed sequentially; only background permuter work overlaps an active target.
Author documents duplicate Claude source submissions, generic stall handling and discarded partial permuter improvements.
